stem: Five distinct books are to be arranged on a shelf such that two particular books, Book-P and Book-Q, must each occupy one of the odd-numbered positions (positions 1, 3, or 5). In how many ways can all five books be arranged?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Choose and assign 2 of the 3 odd positions to Book-P and Book-Q: P(3,2) = 3 x 2 = 6 ways. The remaining 3 books fill the remaining 3 positions in 3! = 6 ways. Total = 6 x 6 = 36.
Computed 3 x 2 x 3! x 2 = 72, inserting a spurious extra factor of 2 (perhaps counting each arrangement twice in error).
Computed C(3,2) x 3! = 3 x 6 = 18, using the combination C(3,2) for placing P and Q (treating their two positions as an unordered pair and losing the 2! factor for P vs Q assignment).
Computed C(3,2) x 2! = 3 x 2 = 6 for P and Q, then multiplied by the remaining 2 positions instead of 3!, yielding 6 x 2 = 12.

explanation: Positions 1, 3, 5 are the odd positions. Book-P and Book-Q must each take one of these 3 odd positions. Since P and Q are distinct, this is an ordered selection: P(3,2) = 3 x 2 = 6 ways. The remaining 3 books fill the remaining 3 positions (positions 2, 4, and whichever odd position is left) in 3! = 6 ways. Total = 6 x 6 = 36.

explanation_sections.punchline: Restricted positions first: assign P and Q to 2 of 3 odd slots as an ordered selection, then place the rest freely.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify: linear arrangement, position-type restriction on two specific elements. Step 1 - place P and Q in odd positions (order matters since P and Q are different books): P(3,2) = 3!/(3-2)! = 6. Step 2 - remaining 3 books in remaining 3 positions: 3! = 6. Multiply: 6 x 6 = 36.
explanation_sections.lesson: Restricted-position problems: handle the constrained elements with a permutation (not combination), then fill the rest freely.
explanation_sections.timing: 35 seconds: P(3,2) x 3! = 6 x 6 = 36. Trap: using C(3,2) = 3 instead of P(3,2) = 6, giving 18.
